cifteminare.name: Çifte Minareli Medrese
cifteminare.slogan: Two fluted minarets over a Seljuk princess's school.
cifteminare.line: Its portal inscription credits Khudavand Khatun, daughter of Sultan Kayqubad I, and may have been the model for Sivas's Gök Medrese.

yakutiye.name: Yakutiye Medrese
yakutiye.slogan: A Mongol-era school whose portal is carved like lace.
yakutiye.line: Ordered in 1310 by the Ilkhanid governor Hoca Yakut, it is now Erzurum's museum of Turkish and Islamic art.

erzurumkalesi.name: Erzurum Castle
erzurumkalesi.slogan: The oldest stones in town, watching over the plateau.
erzurumkalesi.line: The Byzantines first raised a fortress here in 422 to hold off the Persians, making it the oldest site in Erzurum.

tortumselalesi.name: Tortum Waterfall
tortumselalesi.slogan: Turkey's tallest fall, roaring loudest in May and June.
tortumselalesi.line: A landslide dammed the Tortum valley, and the river found a new way over a fault: a 48-metre drop.

osvank.name: Öşvank Monastery
osvank.slogan: A Georgian cathedral with painted walls, high in Turkish hills.
osvank.line: Built in the second half of the 10th century by the Georgian Bagrationi princes, it is said to be the model for Kutaisi's Bagrati Cathedral.
